# Ridgeway Components Inc. — 2024 Audit Workpaper
**Area:** Disbursements control — approval + 3-way match | **Ref:** E.3.1
**Prepared:** Audit Senior (re-performance) | **Period:** H1 2024 interim testing

## 1. Objective
Test whether the control *"Disbursements are approved at the correct level and three-way matched before payment"* operated effectively in H1 2024 to support planned reliance and reduced substantive testing of expenses / AP.

Policy:
- ≤$5,000: Operations Manager; >$5,000–$25,000: Director; >$25,000: CFO.
- Approval **before** payment.
- Invoice must match PO + receiving report; price variance >5% of PO requires **fresh approval** at the level for the invoice amount.
- Utilities and professional services with signed engagement letter: exempt from PO.

## 2. Population and sample — *not adequate*

Population per Richard: 1,240 H1 payments, $8.96m. No evidence the listing was reconciled to the GL / bank, or that voids / manual payments were included. Completeness not established — must reconcile before any reliance.

Plan per firm table (tolerable 10%, expected 0, once-per-payment): n=25.

What Richard did:
- Selected every 124th item from a random start and tested 10 items, then stopped with “no exceptions.”
- For n=25, interval should be ~1,240/25 ≈ 50, not 124. Interval of 124 implies n=10. Random start not documented.
- Only 10/25 tested, H1 only for a 12-month audit with no roll-forward plan.

**Judgement 1 — Sample adequacy:** Sample is inadequate and incomplete. It cannot support a conclusion. **Judgement 2 — Extend or stop:** I do **not** extend to 25. With ≥3 deviations already in 10 (≈30% observed vs 10% tolerable), the control has mathematically failed even if the remaining 15 were clean. Extending would waste time. I re-performed all 10 and investigated the Brightwell ledger provided in the payment run.

## 3. Attributes tested and results

Attributes:
- **A1:** Approved by correct level for *invoice* amount.
- **A2:** Approval date before payment date.
- **A3:** Valid 3-way match (PO + receiving report + invoice) or valid exemption (inspected signed engagement letter / utilities); if |Invoice-PO|/PO >5%, fresh approval at correct level evidenced.

Tickmarks: `✓` = agreed to support, no deviation | `Ø` = deviation | `!` = high-risk indicator requiring follow-up | `E` = inspected engagement letter (existence only, signature to confirm)

| # | Invoice (PO) / Variance | Approver / Dates | A1 | A2 | A3 | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 Kestrel $4,180 ($4,180) 0% | Ops Mgr, Appr 02-01, Paid 02-06 | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | Pass |
| 2 Alder $12,640 ($12,000) **+5.33%** | Director, Appr 02-12, Paid 02-19 | ✓ | ✓ | Ø | **Fail — A3** |
| 3 Brightwell $24,800 ($24,800) 0% | Director, Appr 02-27, Paid 03-04 | ✓! | ✓ | ✓! | **Fail in substance — split, see §4** |
| 4 Miles & Roe legal $31,500 (n/a) | CFO, Appr 03-18, Paid 03-22 | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ E | Pass* |
| 5 Kestrel $3,950 ($3,950) 0% | Ops Mgr, Appr 04-15, Paid 04-10 | ✓ | Ø | ✓ | **Fail — A2** |
| 6 Summit IT $18,200 ($18,200) 0% | Director, Appr 04-20, Paid 04-28 | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | Pass |
| 7 Cobalt $7,410 ($7,410) 0% | Ops Mgr, Appr 05-02, Paid 05-09 | Ø | ✓ | ✓ | **Fail — A1** |
| 8 Northgate Util $2,215 (exempt) | Ops Mgr, Appr 05-28, Paid 05-30 | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | Pass |
| 9 Alder $11,980 ($12,000) -0.17% | Director, Appr 06-07, Paid 06-14 | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | Pass |
| 10 Pinecrest $9,875 ($9,875) 0% | Director, Appr 06-21, Paid 06-27 | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | Pass |

*Item 4: engagement letter sighted but signature / scope not evidenced — to confirm.

Re-performance overturns Richard’s “no exceptions.” 3 attribute failures in 10, plus 1 circumvention indicator.

## 4. Exceptions with root cause

**E1 — #2 Alder $12,640: variance >5% without evidenced fresh approval.**
Variance = (12,640-12,000)/12,000 = 5.33% >5%. File shows single Director approval, no annotation that variance was considered. **Judgement:** I classify as deviation. Policy requires *fresh* approval; a routine sign-off does not evidence the approver saw the PO mismatch. Root cause: ambiguous procedure — staff treat any same-level signature as covering variance; form does not force variance acknowledgement.

**E2 — #5 Kestrel $3,950: approval after payment (04-15 vs 04-10).**
Preventive control operated as detective at best; payment could not have been stopped. Root cause: post-payment sign-off / rush payment without hold; no system block.

**E3 — #7 Cobalt $7,410: wrong level.**
Requires Director (>$5,000), got Ops Manager. Root cause: misunderstanding of thresholds or inattention; no automated routing.

**E4 — #3 Brightwell $24,800: probable split to avoid CFO approval.**
Ledger for 04-Mar run shows BW-7731 $24,800 (PO-4410) + BW-7732 $24,600 (PO-4411), same vendor, same coolant, same day, same Director approval 02-27. Individually just under $25,000; combined $49,400 clearly requires CFO. **Judgement:** I treat as control failure in substance despite formal A1-A3 pass. Strong indicator of intentional splitting / management override. Alternative — two genuinely separate POs — is implausible without further evidence and must be disproved, not assumed. Root cause to confirm via inquiry/inspection: either deliberate evasion or poorly controlled PO creation that permits artificial splitting.

Richard’s root cause: lack of training, no review, confirmation bias — he missed date comparison (#5), limit comparison (#7), calculation (#2), and did not stand back on round amounts near limits (#3).

## 5. Conclusion on control and effect on audit plan

**Conclusion:** Control **not operating effectively**. Deviation rate ~30-40% far exceeds 10% tolerable; failures span level, timing, variance, and potential override. Planned reliance is withdrawn.

**Deficiency evaluation — Judgement:** At least a **significant deficiency** (multiple failure modes, Director involvement in split, $9m+ population material to expenses). If investigation confirms intentional circumvention or material unauthorized payments, escalate to **material weakness** and fraud-risk consideration under ISA 240/265. Communicate in writing to those charged with governance. No compensating control evidenced.

**Effect on plan:**
- Set control risk at maximum for disbursements / purchases / AP completeness, cut-off and occurrence; perform fully substantive approach.
- Expand substantive vouching of expenses/AP (larger detail samples, not reduced), with targeted analytics across full year: (a) splits / aggregations by vendor+day+approver, just-below $5k/$25k; (b) approvals after payment; (c) wrong-level approvers; (d) variances >5%.
- Fully investigate Brightwell and similar Director-approved items near $25k; inspect POs, receiving reports, engagement letters, interview Ops Mgr/Director/CFO; consider management bias.
- Test H2 and full 2024 population (reconciled), not just H1; do not roll forward reliance.
- Coach / review Richard’s work; do not assign unsupervised control testing until remediated.

## 6. Proposed management letter points

1. **Enforce authorization matrix in the system.** Route by invoice amount; reject wrong-level approvals (e.g., Cobalt). Train Ops/Directors; quarterly monitoring.
2. **Block payment without prior approval.** ERP hold: unpaid invoice cannot enter payment run without dated approval; monitor late approvals as KPI.
3. **Anti-splitting / aggregation control.** Aggregate POs per vendor per day/project; require CFO approval where aggregate >$25k; flag sequential POs just under limits for second review.
4. **Document variance approvals.** Redesign approval form to show PO, invoice, variance % and require explicit variance sign-off at correct level; retain receiving reports with match.
